title: Potassium Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Potassium Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Potassium deficiency shows on the old leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Potassium deficiency in plants starts on the old, lower leaves. Potassium runs the plant's water use by opening and closing the pores of the leaf, and it switches on many enzymes. It moves sugars into grain, fruit and roots, so it decides grain weight, fruit size and quality. It also keeps stems strong against lodging and helps the crop stand up to drought, pests and diseases. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Leaves with brown, scorched edges (avocado): the classic potassium shortage sign on older leaves

blocks.text: Potassium is very mobile in the plant and shifts from old leaves to new growth when the supply runs low. So the scorched edges show first on the older, lower leaves and climb up the plant if the shortage goes on.
Potassium deficiency symptoms

The edges and tips of older leaves turn yellow, then brown and dry, as if burned. While the middle of the leaf stays green. Brown spots may appear on the leaves, stems grow thin and weak, and plants lodge more easily. Rice plants look dark green with brown leaf edges, and many grains stay empty. In banana the old leaves yellow and die early, the midrib tip bends down, and bunches and fingers stay small.
Potassium deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [potassium in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#potassium).

blocks.text: What causes potassium deficiency

Sandy soils and old, highly weathered acid soils hold little potassium, and heavy rain or typhoon floods wash it out. Heavy use of urea or 16 20 0 with little or no potash drains the soil. So does hauling away or burning straw. Every harvest carries potassium away, and PCA surveys found it short in some coconut areas. Poorly drained, waterlogged soils and soils very rich in magnesium also keep roots from taking it up.
How to be sure it is potassium

Magnesium shortage also starts on old leaves, but it yellows the leaf between the veins instead of burning the edges. In banana, manganese shortage looks alike but starts on the young leaves. Salt damage from too much fertilizer also scorches leaf edges. A soil test for exchangeable potassium, from the BSWM Soil Test Kit or a DA Regional Soils Laboratory, shows if the soil is short. A leaf tissue test confirms it. In lowland rice, the PhilRice MOET pots show missing potassium as short, poorly growing plants.
How to fix potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash (0 0 60), sulfate of potash (0 0 50) or 14 14 14. Return straw, ash and compost. For coconut palms 5 years and older, a typical PCA rate is 1.5 to 2 kg of muriate of potash per palm a year. Let the soil test set the rate. On saline soils split the dose or use sulfate of potash, which adds less salt.
A potassium nitrate (13 0 44) spray helps vegetables and fruit trees recover for a short time. Use it as a quick help and keep the soil dose, which does the main work.

How to keep potassium deficiency away

Replace the potassium each harvest removes, and keep straw in the field instead of burning it, or spread the ash evenly. Balance potash with nitrogen and phosphorus so the crop never runs on urea alone.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: Too much potash holds back magnesium uptake, so heavy potash can bring on magnesium shortage, mostly on sandy soils. Muriate of potash also adds salt, which can scorch leaf edges on saline soil.

blocks.text: Potassium deficiency questions

items.q: What does potassium deficiency look like?
items.a: The edges and tips of the older leaves turn yellow, then brown and dry, as if scorched. Stems grow weak, plants lodge, and grain, fruit or bunches stay small.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for potassium deficiency?
items.a: Muriate of potash (0 0 60) is the usual and lowest cost choice. Sulfate of potash (0 0 50) suits salty soils, and a complete 14 14 14 carries potassium in smaller amounts.

items.q: Can I use salt instead of potash for coconut?
items.a: Salt supplies chlorine, which coconut needs, but it has no potassium. The PCA guide says to use muriate of potash, not salt, where the soil lacks potassium.

items.q: Why are my banana leaves turning yellow and drying from the tips?
items.a: Potassium shortage is a common cause, starting on the oldest leaves with yellow to orange tips that turn brown. Check with a soil or leaf test, because magnesium shortage and salt damage can look similar.
